newsitem.title: USA: Total World finds four acquisition targets.
newsitem.headline: Total World finds four acquisition targets.

text.p: Total World Telecommunications Inc on Thursday said it identified four companies as potential acquisitions and attributed its fiscal first-quarter loss of $0.77 a share to costs related to two previous acquisitions.
For the previous first quarter, the company reported a loss per share of $0.90.
The company declined to name the targets.

The company, which changed its name in October from International Standards Group Ltd, said it would focus on its telecommunications operation and planned to sell or spin off its real estate and mortgage companies.
Total World, a switch-based long-distance carrier, reported that its first-quarter revenue increased almost sevenfold to $10.7 million from $1.6 million in the first quarter of the previous year.
The company attributed the revenue increase to the acquisition of Total National Telecommunications Inc.

It said the $0.77 loss per share reflected certain operational start-up costs for its recent acquisitions of Southwestern Long Distance Inc and N'Touch, along with dividend payments to preferred stockholders.
